data.text: Augmented reality devices are categorized into headsets and glasses, handheld devices, projection-based systems, spatial augmented reality, head-up displays, and AR contact lenses. Examples include the Microsoft HoloLens, Google Glass, smartphones, and interactive projectors. Head-up displays are typically found in cars, while AR contact lenses are the latest technology being explored. These categories serve various application domains, such as education, retail, industrial design, healthcare, and medical development.
points: Augmented reality devices are categorized into headsets and glasses, handheld devices, projection-based systems, spatial augmented reality, head-up displays, and AR contact lenses.
Examples include the Microsoft HoloLens, Google Glass, Vuzix Blade Glasses, smartphones, tablets, and Nintendo devices.
Projection-based systems and spatial augmented reality include interactive projectors, AR sandboxes, projection mapping software, laser projectors, and projection keyboards.
Head-up displays are typically found in cars, while AR contact lenses are the latest technology being explored.
These AR categories serve various application domains, including education, retail, industrial design, healthcare, and medical development.

data.text: AR headsets are generally larger and more immersive than VR headsets, providing a wider field of view and blending real-world content with digital content. These headsets typically include built-in sensors like cameras and depth sensors, whereas VR headsets often have fewer components because they do not need to provide a real-world view. Additionally, AR headsets can integrate digital content with a real-world view and support interactions through eye movements, voice commands, and hand motions.
points: AR headsets are generally larger and more immersive, providing a wider field of view and blending real-world content with digital content.
AR headsets typically include built-in sensors, such as cameras and depth sensors.

AR headsets can integrate digital content with a real-world view and support interactions through eye movements, voice commands, and hand motions.

data.text: AR smart glasses are lighter and more comfortable than AR headsets but provide simpler heads-up display overlays instead of 3D holograms. Examples of these devices include Google Glass, Vuzix's Blade, Epson glasses, and Magic Leap glasses. Handheld AR devices like smartphones and tablets are the most common and accessible options, using cameras to overlay digital content on real-world images via marker-based or markerless technologies.
points: AR smart glasses are lighter and more comfortable than AR headsets but are less immersive and less powerful.
Smart glasses provide simpler heads-up display overlays whereas headsets provide full 3D holograms.
Examples of smart glasses include Google Glass, Vuzix's Blade, Epson glasses, and Magic Leap glasses.
Handheld AR devices like smartphones and tablets are the most common and accessible AR devices.
Handheld AR devices use a camera to capture real-world images and overlay digital content using marker-based or markerless technologies.

data.text: Spatial augmented reality (AR) devices use projectors to overlay virtual content onto the physical environment. These systems are not tied to the user and allow multiple people to interact with the content simultaneously. Implementing these systems requires understanding the geometry and lighting of the environment, which is why they are used in various domains like education, art, and entertainment.
points: Spatial augmented reality (AR) devices use projectors to overlay virtual content onto the physical environment.
These devices are not tied to the user and allow multiple people to interact with the content simultaneously.
Implementing these systems requires understanding the geometry and lighting of the environment using sensors or computer vision.
Categories of spatial AR include interactive projectors, air sandboxes, projection keyboards, and projection mapping.
Spatial AR systems are used in various fields such as education, medical training, and entertainment.

data.text: Head-up displays project images onto transparent surfaces and are commonly used in cars and aircraft. While current AR hardware is often bulky or difficult to hold, AR contact lenses are an emerging technology that superimposes information directly onto a wearer's field of vision. These lenses can contain miniaturized components, but their effects on the user are not well known or researched.
points: Head-up displays project images onto transparent surfaces and are commonly used in cars and aircraft.
Many current AR hardware systems are bulky, require elaborate setups, or can be difficult to hold for long periods.
AR contact lenses are a future wearable technology that superimposes digital information directly onto a wearer's field of vision.
These lenses can contain miniaturized components, but their effects on the user are not well known or researched.
